sections.title: Imports and language input rule
sections.what: Brings in the helpers and defines the rule that accepts only supported language codes and rejects any extra fields.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond limiting the input to supported values.

sections.name: limiter
sections.title: Language change limit and save
sections.what: Allows 30 changes per address per minute, saves the language on the account and in a one-year cookie, and returns the result.
sections.why: Likely reason: the limit stops abuse and the cookie covers visitors who are not signed in.
sections.watch_out: The cookie lasts one year, so a visitor keeps this language on the same browser until it expires or they change it.

summary: Saves the fan's chosen language in a browser cookie for everyone, and also on the account when they are signed in.
purpose: Powers the language switch in the top navigation.
why: The comment says the cookie is for all visitors and the account value is for signed-in users, so the choice survives across devices.
how: 1) Checks the per-address limit. 2) Checks the language is one of the supported ones. 3) Saves it to the account if signed in. 4) Sets a one-year cookie and returns the choice.
inputs: A POST with a language code. The user comes from the session if signed in.
outputs: A JSON result with the language and where it was stored, plus a language cookie.
risks: The limit is per address, so users on the same network share it.
debug: If the language does not stick, check the cookie name in the i18n provider and the account save function.
